text:
marie: Observing large NCCL throughput regression in eucentral after OFED/firmware rollout — many jobs falling back to TCP. Allreduce rates dropped ~8x. Anyone else?
infra-bot: deploy-bot: OFED/firmware rollout to eu-central finished 2026-03-02T03:12Z (batch-efa-2026-03).
tyler: Confirmed on p3/p4 pools. nvidia driver + CUDA seem fine. NCCL logs: 'transport (rdma) unavailable, falling back to TCP' in multiple job logs.
sachin: Can you paste nccl-tests / microbench numbers and the stack (kernel/driver/OFED/firmware)?
marie: nccl-tests (8 nodes x16GB): was ~240 GB/s pre-rollout, now ~28 GB/s. Kernel: 6.5.4, mlx5 fw: 18.32.256, OFED: 5.1.2, NVIDIA driver: 535.54, CUDA: 12.2.
eli: This smells like a PMTU/fragmentation issue after the mlx5 firmware change. If RDMA packets are being dropped or ICMP 'fragmentation needed' is blocked, NCCL will time out and fall back to TCP leading to massive perf loss. Check dmesg for mlx5 errors and look for ICMP messages on path.
tyler: Ran quick tests: iperf3 (TCP) shows ~10-20 Gbps on affected nodes, iperf3 -u shows very poor UDP. tcpdump captured ICMP frag-needed from an intermediate switch for packets >1500. ethtool -k shows GSO/GRO offloads inconsistent on a few NICs.
sachin: Workaround options: 1) revert OFED/firmware on a small canary set; 2) force MTU/clamp/MSS adjustments; 3) vendor engagement. Reverting seems fastest to validate.
andrew: Customer impact/cost: ~30% of scheduled distributed training jobs seeing >3x runtime. If this persists, estimated incremental GPU cost ~+$12k/week on on-demand capacity and SLA churn for Dedicated customers. We should throttle the rollout.
infra-bot: incident-bot created INF-2026-032: "eu-central OFED/firmware regression affecting RDMA/NCCL" assigned to eng-infra oncall.
marie: I'm rolling back OFED on 4 canary nodes now: sudo apt install --allow-downgrades mlx-ofed=5.0.8 && systemctl restart mlx5-mods; will run nccl-tests after restart.
tyler: Also ping support/sales to avoid onboarding new Dedicated deployments in eu-central until we confirm.
sachin: I'll file vendor ticket with Mellanox: include /var/log/dmesg, ethtool -S, rdma-core logs, and pcap: /tmp/efa-pmtu-euc.pcap.gz. Include exact fw and OFED hashes.
eli: If rollback restores perf, add a preflight netperf + nccl-tests gate to the firmware rollout pipeline. Also add kernel compatibility check for 6.5 vs 6.1 series — some drivers had changes in skb fragmentation behavior.
marie: Rollback complete on canaries: nccl-tests allreduce back to ~230 GB/s on the 4 nodes. Pausing remaining rollout. Opening PR to pause pipeline: infra/fw-rollout#129.
andrew: Good catch. Let's also estimate a rollback window and sync with capacity planning (possible job reschedules). I'll coordinate with capacity to move urgent jobs.
marie: Next steps: vendor ticket + expanded captures, pause rollout, add preflight checks (netperf UDP + nccl allreduce), and a communication note to Dedicated customers in eucentral. Posting runbook updates in #eng-infra. :thumbsup:
